title: Wreck and Compass
premise: Jonah Winterbourne, a disgraced railroad engineer hiding in the northern bush with his map of abandoned lines, joins a salvage crew sent upriver when an expedition stops answering the radio. What he finds is a settlement built by the vanished expedition, ruled by a charismatic surveyor who has weaponized the old rail infrastructure and Jonah's own forgotten past to control the valley. As the monsoon traps them with a leaking boat and the settlement's enigmatic doctor, Wren, torn between her oath to the community and her growing love for Jonah, he must choose between reclaiming the identity he fled and destroying the power built from it. They escape downriver through the calving glacier's brief open channel, burning the map that made them both prisoners, and vanish into the wilderness together.
about_author: Mirabel Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former bush pilot who spent a decade ferrying supplies to remote river settlements before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who go looking for the edge of the map and find themselves there instead.

chapters.title: The Silence on Channel Nine
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. When the survey expedition upriver goes silent, salvage broker Odile hires Jonah for his forbidden knowledge of the closed rail lines, and he reluctantly boards the leaky riverboat Kestrel. Flashbacks reveal the engineering scandal that drove him into hiding. Emotional beat: dread masked as pragmatism, as Jonah realizes the river leads back toward the life he buried.

chapters.title: The Town That Answers to One Voice
chapters.summary: POV alternating Jonah and Wren. They find the missing expedition absorbed into Meridian, a settlement where surveyor Cassius Hale rules through control of the rail junction and rationed radio access. Wren, the settlement doctor, secretly treats Jonah's injured crewmate and begins questioning Hale's account. Emotional beat: unease curdling into recognition, as Hale greets Jonah by a name no one should know.

chapters.title: What the Glacier Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Wren, with Jonah's interludes. Hale reveals Jonah designed Meridian's infrastructure years ago under a different identity, and offers him co-leadership if he helps seal the valley before monsoon flood. Wren and Jonah plan escape, but a betrayal by Odile forces them to steal the Kestrel during the storm's peak. Emotional beat: love declared in the space between duty and ruin, as Wren burns her medical oath papers to cut the settlement's power.

chapters.title: The Brief Opening
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Racing the flood and Hale's armed launch, they run the rapids toward the glacier calving channel, which opens for only hours. Jonah uses his engineer's knowledge to wreck Hale's pursuit at the old rail bridge, choosing to destroy his own work rather than rule it. They slip through the ice-choked narrows as Meridian's lights fail behind them. Emotional beat: hard-won peace, two people finally visible to each other and no one else.
